title: The Loose Contact
premise: Wendell Underhill, a disgraced hostage negotiator hiding in witness protection after the botched exchange that killed a young teller, discovers the safe house he's lived in for three years listed online — interior photos and all, including the wall where he's taped his obsessive reconstruction of the incident. The listing is bait from the broker who laundered the ransom money, a man who knows Wendell kept a recording proving a police captain orchestrated the whole robbery. Hunted by both the captain's cleaners and federal handlers who may be compromised, Wendell must trade the tape for his life, but chooses instead to weaponize it, walking back into the negotiation room he swore off. In the end he trades the recording not for safety but for the captain's confession, surviving at the cost of his anonymity forever — the price of survival is that he can never stop being a negotiator.
about_author: Felix Vane spent a decade as a crisis-line volunteer before turning to fiction, drawing on the strange intimacy of talking strangers back from the edge. He writes thrillers about people whose professional calm is a thin shell over private ruin.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Insomniac and rigid with routine, Wendell finds the safe house on a real estate site — every room photographed, including his evidence wall, blurred just enough to be recognizable. His handler dismisses it as a database leak, but Wendell notices the listing agent's name matches an alias from the ransom case. Emotional beat: the floor dropping out of false safety; paranoia sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Open House
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, with an intercut of the broker's. Posing as a curious buyer, Wendell confronts the broker, Dana Reyes, who reveals she was the money launderer's accountant and wants the tape to buy her own way out. She gives him forty-eight hours before she sells the location to the captain's people. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance; two survivors realizing they're each other's leverage.

chapters.title: The Exchange Rate
chapters.summary: Alternating Wendell and Captain Marsh's POVs. Marsh's cleaners hit the house while Wendell is out retrieving the hidden recording; Dana is taken, and Marsh offers Wendell the trade he's been dreading — the tape for Dana's life. Wendell negotiates instead: a face-to-face at the old bank, marshals he no longer trusts watching. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into cold craft; the negotiator fully awake again.

chapters.title: Closing Costs
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. At the bank, Wendell runs the negotiation of his life, baiting Marsh into confessing on a live feed wired to internal affairs and a journalist. Marsh breaks; the cleaners stand down; Dana walks free but vanishes with a copy of everything. Wendell surrenders the original and his protected identity with it. Emotional beat: costly victory — survival achieved, invisibility forfeited, and for the first time in years, he sleeps.
